intended_object: The real plane ℝ² = ℝ × ℝ, used in the library as the plane covering the 2-torus (inferred from the name and the docstring of the aliased `TorusInverse.Plane`: "an abbreviation for `ℝ × ℝ`").
explanation: `Plane` is a local alias for `NavierStokes.TorusInverse.Plane`, which is set at line 375 of `NavierStokes/SmoothFourierData.lean` to `abbrev Plane := ℝ × ℝ`, with the docstring "Plane: an abbreviation for `ℝ × ℝ`". So the definition is exactly the real plane ℝ² that its name describes. It is one particular space, used as the plane covering the 2-torus alongside `Frequency := ℤ × ℤ`, not a general construction written out in a special case, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no separate definition to cite: ℝ² is just the product type ℝ × ℝ. On ℝ × ℝ, Mathlib's norm is the sup norm, not the Euclidean one. That would only matter where Euclidean structure is needed, and it does not affect whether this alias correctly names the plane.
